ceramic.title: Live-Action Spider-Man Spin-Off Silk TV Series Is in the Works at Sony TVovermind
ceramic.snippet:
Live-Action Spider-Man Spin-Off Silk TV Series Is in the Works at Sony by Tom Foster If a character is tied directly to Spider-Man it’s likely that Sony has the rights to them, which would include Cindy Moon, aka Silk . Bitten by the same spider that affected Peter Park, Silk is pretty much like Spider-Man save for the fact that she has a different outfit, doesn’t hide her whole face, and can produce her own organic webbing while Peter had to manufacture his. You might want to argue that Tobey Maguire’s character could produce his own webbing, but seeing as how even Sony has moved on from Maguire and has taken on the idea of making Peter create his own webbing, it’s probably better to simply accept that Silk is the only Spider-person that can produce her own natural webbing at this point. Apparently Silk is being developed into a live-action series that will be bringing the heroine to the small screen for fans to enjoy, though what that will entail isn’t quite known as of yet since the fact is that among the many different Spider-Man-themed individuals, there are backstories, powers, lifestyles, and definitely enemies that have to be considered when talking about each one. As it’s been seen in the comics though there are plenty of enemies to go around and she has shared a couple with Spider-Man, and she’s shared a few moments with him as well apparently.

 A live-action show would be kind of interesting if only because it would be taking the Spider-Man story in a different direction with a new person that has been around for a while but has still been largely unknown to everyone save those that have read the comics.

Sony Confirms The DualShock 4 Controller Will Work On The PS5 But Only With PS4 Games - Stuff South Africa

 Sony confirms the DualShock 4 controller will work on the PS5 but only with PS4 games By Brad Lang Updated:   No Comments   3 Mins Read Share   Facebook   Twitter   LinkedIn   Pinterest   Email 

 You know what, this might be an extremely hot take right now, given how the announcement of the PS5 and all those rad games for it kinda took the world by storm. Look, Ill be the first to say that Im as hype for a new  Ratchet and Clank  and  Spider-Man  game as the next guy, but beyond software the services around the PlayStation 5 are more frustrating than anything else. As an example, while Microsoft is out there toting how the Xbox Series X will offer backwards compatibility of  four generations of games,  Sony took it upon themselves to cherry pick favourites that will be playable on the PS5 at launch with no word yet on even older generations. Now, the announcement that the DualShock 4 will work with the PS5 but, in typical Sony fashion, there are some irritating caveats to the whole thing.

 Now sure, Sony could spin this into a case for PlayStation 5 games needing the newer Dual Sense controller due to all the exclusive features of the new controller those titles will no doubt use. Yet it was the same story for the DualShock 4 and do you have any idea how many games actually made clever use of the touch pad and built-in speaker? Thats right, approximately four and two of them did it badly.

  Of course, the compatibility only becomes more cloudy the more you think about it. Will the DualShock 4 continue to work with PS4 titles that are upgraded onto the PS5?

  Its a real mess of an announcement that was no doubt meant to be quite important for Sony. Its stuff like this that just deflates my excitement for Sonys next-generation. How is a company able to do so many things correctly and yet still fumble such basic stuff like this so easily?

ceramic.title: Techart unveils the World’s First Sony E to Nikon Z Autofocus Adapter - Newsshooter
ceramic.snippet:
Techart unveils the World’s First Sony E to Nikon Z Autofocus Adapter - Newsshooter

 Techart has unveiled their Sony E to Nikon Z Autofocus Adapter (TZE-01) . The new TZE-01 is claimed to be the world’s first autofocus adapter that allows autofocus functionality when using Sony E-mount lenses on Nikon Z6 and Z7 cameras.Im not sure how many people would actually be putting Sony E mount lenses onto a Nikon Z6 or Nikon Z7, but at least you now have the option. 

 The flange distance of Nikon Z-mount is only 2mm shorter than Sony E-mount. According to Techart, this made it extremely difficult to design the adapter. Techart includes connectors of both sides and a PCB board with a chip to “translate” the protocol of the lens and the camera.

  This adapter is developed through reverse engineering. In other words, despite Techarts 100% effort in making this adapter compatible with all the Sony E-mount lenses and Nikon Z-cameras, the adapter is still NOT perfect. This is similar to other AF adapters in the market.

 The Techart adapter enables both Auto Focus & Auto Aperture functions of Sony E mount lenses to be used on Nikon Z6 and Z7. AF-S, AF-C & MF mode are all supported in both still & video shooting. The Face & Eye Detection of Z-mount cameras can also be used, however, this only works in the stills mode. 

 The Techart adapter currently supports most of the Sony, Sigma, Tamron & Zeiss AF lenses with Sony E mounts. This includes popular lenses such as the Tamron 28-75mm, Batis 25mm f/2, Sony 24mm f/1.4 GM and Sigma 35mm f/1.4. Techart is currently working to support more lenses.

 The Techart Sony E to Nikon Z Autofocus Adapter is currently available for pre-order at the Techart official website ( http://www.techartpro.com ). The recommended retail price before tax is $249 USD . Free shipping will be provided during the promotion period. Delivery will start in late June. A 1-year warranty is included with the adapter.

Sony Job Cuts by Segment and Region 2026

<Francesco Riganese>By Francesco RiganeseOctober 10, 20267 Mins Read
<Sony employee statistics 2026 showing workforce decline, business segment headcounts, global distribution, and PlayStation layoffs.>
Sony counted about 94,900 employees on March 31, 2026, against 112,300 a year earlier. This guide to Sony employee statistics breaks that change down by segment, region and subsidiary using Sony’s own filings, and tracks the PlayStation and Bungie cuts announced since 2024.

Sony Employee Statistics

94,900Sony Group employees on March 31, 2026
17,400Fewer employees than on March 31, 2025
103,600Average headcount across fiscal 2025, quarter-end basis
52,600Employees based outside Japan, March 31, 2026
12,300Game & Network Services (PlayStation) employees, March 31, 2026

How Many Employees Does Sony Have in 2026?

Sony Group had about 94,900 employees on March 31, 2026, according to the Form 20-F it filed with the SEC on June 18, 2026. That is the latest year-end count Sony has published.
The total held near 113,000 for three year-ends before the drop. Sony reported 113,000 at March 2023 and March 2024, then 112,300 at March 2025.
Averaged across the four quarter-ends, fiscal 2025 headcount was about 103,600, against 113,300 in fiscal 2024. The group’s financial services arm left the consolidated count on October 1, 2025, halfway through that fiscal year.
Source: Sony Group securities report (EDINET), year-end counts March 2022 to March 2026; Sony Group Form 20-F, fiscal years ended March 31, 2025 and 2026
